questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Somewhere outside Europe

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Best exchange everrr

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - they sent everything on mail

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The main coordinator of the Canadian University was so good at providing us the necessary information and helping out with question

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were a bunch of different residence houses available. However, after filliing out the application, they gave me the options of either Lambton hall and Bayfield hall.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The meal plan catered to all diets (vegetarians, vegans, pescetarians, gluten-free, lactose intolerance, nut allergy etc.). All residence buildings had a kitchen, however, you have to buy kitchen equipment (pots, pans, utensils, etc.) yourselves.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Don't expect to become besties with your roommate. And if you know you love your personal space, apply for the single room in Bayfield hall or single room in an apartment with one roommate in Lambton hall.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Its a bidding system. You get points (I don't remember how many), and then you have to bid on the courses you want. If you really want a course you will have to bid with more of your points. You can also look at the previous years bidding, to see on average how many points the course you want had in order to know how many points to bid. Please bid as soon as you receive the email!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: we received an email explaining the bidding system. And the exchange coordinator at Western Law was there to help (online - email).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: tbh very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: honestly apply for courses as soon as you receive the email and after that don't stress about your courses. If you have any questions, problems etc. just email the exchange coordinator at host university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Law school in Canada, at least the law school I went to, comprises of 3 years. I took 2nd and 3rd year classes

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: So at the Canadian law school they did attendance, particifpation, final paper (essay) and/or sit down exam as a part of my grade. So it would e.g. be 10% attendance, 20% participation, and 70% the final paper (essay).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: environmental law (highly recommend), mental health law (very interesting), condominium law, and bankruptcy & insolvency law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Definitely environmental law, since the prof was VERY down to earth and the structure of that class was SO loose. 
And also mental health law because the prof (DeMelo) was very good at her job and the course was actually very interesting. Another major pro about these two courses is that they have a final paper (essay) as an exam

questions.answer: Duvet, pillowcase, bedsheets, towels + cleaning surplies (thought they provided us the stuff but no you have to buy that yourself except a vaccum cleaner, broom and trash bags)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Duvet, pillowcase and bedsheets from Western University onlineshop

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: everything from sport activities/clubs to creative stuff such as knitting club etc. They also had a wine and beer club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: hmm probably the law knitting club - it was really fun. But also just the activities the different dining halls are hosting sometimes such as pumpkin carving evening or tote bag painting etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to downtown London and explore the nightlife (bars), and go to hockey and basketball games. AAAND go on trips - Vancouver, Banff, NYC, Toronto, Niagara Falls, MMontreal, Quebec City, Ottowa etc..

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Honestly join a bunch of clubs and just be open and friendly

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: smalltalk - I had to get used to it at the beginning buuuut now I loveeee it!!!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the openness, friendliness, and the smaltalk!!!!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- be open and ready to meet new people 
- try and connect with your roommate but if it's not possible dont force it
- relax and enjoy every second of the exchange!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Your Western onecard is your buscard. 
Bring your own pillow and bedsheets + pillowcase.
I you don't have the mealplan buy grocery from Loblaws -

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the lovely people I've met + all the friends I've gotten

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: figuring out my courses after two of my courses were cancelled + dropped a course. However, the host exchange coordinator at the host university was so sweet and helpful, so honestly if this happens to you, dont stress about it - just email the exchange coordinator at the host university

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
